“all of humanity’s problems stem from man’s inability to sit quietly in a room alone.”blaise pascal

making religion cool again.

why religion? because it's the oldest technology on earth for being okay.

people with a practice live longer, worry less, and know who they are when everything else is loud. five thousand years of testing. nobody's built anything better.

cool isn't loud. cool is the one person in the room who isn't rattled. that's what a practice gets you. that's the whole flex.

for five thousand years, every people on earth built the same thing: a way to sit down, shut up, and remember what matters. we threw it out in one generation and replaced it with a feed. was that the plan?

The founding class

your door has a voice. you already know it.

eight people with no time, taking the time. in your ear for every lesson, in the faith they grew up in. not a gig — it matters to them.

eight doors. one hill.

Christianity, Catholicism, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism — or none of them, which we call my own path. read by people you actually listen to. built for the kid who'd never go in, the parent who wishes they would, and the house that does Christmas and Hanukkah.

your door is yours. we teach it from your own texts, in your own words, checked by scholars of your tradition. you don't need a religion to come in. change it anytime. walk two.

we don't care which door. we care that you have one. we don't compare. we don't guilt. we don't write your prayers. we don't sell your faith.

one human race.

different doors. same house. one rule every single one of them landed on.

every religion on earth landed on the same move: treat people the way you want to be treated. nobody's ever beaten it.

be good to each other and everybody wins. all of us. the whole planet. not a vibe — a plan.

the golden rule is undefeated.

we keep the studies on the research page, not the front door. the kid isn't here because JAMA says so.

infinite hill curious?
FAQs

Do I have to pick a religion?

no. pick a door, or my own path — no tradition attached. change anytime.

Can my school use it?

soon. a teacher tries it free for a term; the school licenses it for less than the textbook it replaces; students never pay. a faith school teaches its own door; any other school teaches religious literacy across all eight. classroom codes, assignments, a progress view, a certificate at every lookout. launching after the pilot.

Can I build my own path?

yes. your home door is yours, and you can visit any other door for a session — a friend's, a partner's, your mother-in-law's. every visit is one door, taught properly, by that door's own texts and people. the path across doors is yours. the sessions never blend. we'd rather you learn your father-in-law's greeting than invent one.

We're an interfaith family. Which door?

both. the table (a planned family plan) holds different doors at one table. the kids can walk two. nobody has to pick.

Is infinite hill a nonprofit?

no. it's a company, so it can pay for itself and never has to beg. part of what it earns goes to the infinite hill foundation, a separate nonprofit (in formation). and when giving opens, anything you give inside the app will go there in full.

Who checks the lessons?

a keeper of that one tradition. see the keepers, above.

Do I have to start from the beginning?

no. two minutes of quick questions puts you where you belong. nobody starts from zero twice.

How long is it?

year one is the mountain — five camps, about a lesson a day. years two to five are the ranges: the texts underneath, the stories, the saints, the sources. some people stay five years.

What happens if I miss a day?

a rest day covers it. your streak grows one lesson a day, with rest days built in, because every tradition knows rest. you start with two and earn one back every week. if a streak does break, two lessons in a day within three days earns it back, never for money. your days on the hill and your place on the path never reset.

Is it for kids?

everyone. under-13s join through a parent's table, on the parent's phone. no messages, no strangers, no ads.

what it feels like

it plays like a game.
it's taught like a faith.

pick your door. you guess, you tap, you say it back, and the lesson lights up when you get it. then the quiet part: a breath, and one line to carry.

  • we score learning, never faith. points for knowing a word. never for praying, never for believing.
  • the quiet moments stay quiet. the breath, the sit and your line to carry have no clock to beat and no score.
  • every lesson is read by a scholar from that tradition before it's final.
